verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.speaker: Vishnu
verse.setting: Vishnu explains to the frightened gods where fear comes from.
verse.sanskrit: दीनताजं भयं माने गुणे खलभयं खलु । भयं निन्दकजं शक्तौ विद्यायां वादिनं भयम् ॥
verse.line: Honour fears disgrace, virtue fears the wicked, power fears critics, learning fears debate. Every gain brings a fear.
verse.translation: In honour lies the fear of being brought low; in virtue, the fear of the wicked; in power, the fear of critics; in learning, the fear of rival debaters.
verse.why: Every gain brings its own fear; holding things lightly is the way out.

prasang.title: Vishnu on where fear comes from
prasang.summary: The frightened gods ask Vishnu how to become fearless. He explains that every possession carries its own fear (the body fears age, wealth fears thieves, power fears critics) and that only dispassion is free of fear; then he restates Bhagavad Gita 2.14-15 on enduring pleasure and pain.
prasang.lesson: Every gain brings its own fear; holding things lightly is the way out.

verse.meaning: Vishnu is speaking to the frightened gods who have just lost their power. He tells them that every gain carries its own fear. The body fears age, wealth fears thieves, power fears critics, and learning fears debate. Nothing you hold is free of worry, so the only way out is to hold things lightly.
verse.for_you: Yesterday you named the storm. Today, see that the rating is not the true fear. The fear is of losing what you have built, of the life you have made. The rating is just the shape that fear takes right now.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
verse.line: Your work is yours to do; the results are not yours to hold. Don't let that make you stop.
verse.translation: Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to doing nothing.
verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

story.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
story.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
story.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
story.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

script: Your mind is at two in the morning. It is wired and terrified, and you are holding the phone like it is the only thing keeping your wife safe. The fear of a bad rating is not just a job risk. It is a storm that will not let you rest.

Arjuna is on the battlefield. He has asked Krishna how a person can practice yoga and keep their mind steady, but he feels his own mind is a wild horse. Krishna listens, and Arjuna tells him that the mind is restless, turbulent and powerful. And Krishna agrees, but he tells Arjuna that it is not about fighting the mind. Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

The mind is a force of nature. It is not a machine you can turn off. When you try to force it to stop checking, it only fights harder. The practice is not about winning a battle with your thoughts. It is about learning to hold the mind steady through repetition, and then releasing it. This is easier said than done, because every time you put the phone down, the fear screams that the visa is slipping away. But the mind can be trained.
Tonight, when the phone buzzes, let the fear be there. Do not try to fix it. Just notice the storm inside you, and let your hand rest. The visa is not decided in the middle of the night.
The mind is a storm. You do not have to hold the wind.

depth.life: You are at two in the morning with the phone in your hand, and the fear feels like a storm. You are living inside a visa that feels like a life sentence, checking for a bad rating that could break everything. You are wired, terrified, and there is no weekend that is truly yours.
depth.points: The mind is not a machine you can shut off. It is restless, stormy, and stubborn by nature, and trying to force it into silence only makes it fight back. The restlessness is not your failure. It is the mind's nature.
depth.practice: Place the phone face down on the table and sit with your hands on your lap. Watch the thoughts come and go without reaching for the screen again.
depth.question: What would it feel like to let the storm pass without fighting it?
